items.title: SWOT analysis is often misused as a sorting exercise
items.claim: SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) emerged from Albert Humphrey's work at Stanford in the 1960s-70s. What's the standard critique?

options.text: It is a complete strategic plan
SWOT identifies factors but provides no method to translate them into strategy; without TOWS-style cross-pairing (S-O, S-T, W-O, W-T), it's just four bullet-point lists
It can only be used for new ventures

items.reveal:
Heinz Weihrich's 1982 TOWS matrix paired Strengths with Opportunities (offensive strategies), Strengths with Threats (defensive), Weaknesses with Opportunities (improvement), and Weaknesses with Threats (mitigation).

The core SWOT critique is that without this step, the framework lists factors without forcing a strategic choice. Most student SWOTs stop at the list stage — which is descriptive, not strategic.
items.why: SWOT looks like analysis but often delivers sorting. The strategic value is in the combinations across quadrants.

items.title: Accounting profit and economic profit measure different things
items.claim: A bakery reports £80,000 accounting profit. The owner could earn £50,000 in alternative employment and £15,000 by renting out the premises. What is the economic profit?
items.reveal:
Accounting profit deducts only explicit costs. Economic profit also deducts opportunity costs — the next-best foregone returns to the owner's time and assets. Here: £80,000 - £50,000 - £15,000 = £15,000.

A business with positive accounting profit but negative economic profit is destroying value relative to alternatives. The distinction was formalised by Alfred Marshall in his 'Principles of Economics' (1890).
items.why: A firm reporting profit on its income statement may still be the wrong use of the owner's resources. Accounting standards weren't designed to answer that question.

items.title: Profitable businesses fail when cash runs out
items.claim: A construction firm books £5 million revenue and £500,000 profit in 2023 but customers pay 120 days after invoicing while suppliers demand 30 days. What is the most likely outcome?

options.text: Strong cash position because of the reported profit
A cash flow gap large enough to threaten survival, despite profitability — overtrading
Profit and cash will be identical
Suppliers must accept 120-day payment by law

items.reveal:
Carillion, the UK construction giant, reported £147 million profit in 2016 and collapsed in January 2018 with £1.5 billion of debt. A large part of the gap between profit and cash came from long receivable cycles on government contracts combined with aggressive revenue recognition.

'Profit is opinion; cash is fact' is an accounting saying with an empirical basis. The UK Insolvency Service reports that 80%+ of business failures involve a cash-flow rather than profitability problem.
items.why: Reported profit can lead, lag or diverge from cash entirely. Working capital management is often what separates surviving and failing firms.
